column1: # bugs_open/029 — PRESERVED EVIDENCE. Exported 2026-08-20 from the live DB.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: awaited_requests deletes terminal rows at processed_at + 7 days
# begins deleting 2026-08-24 00:32 and rolls through that day. After that the wedge has
# NO retained instances anywhere: orchestration_states purged its rows on 2026-08-19.
# SCOPE: every awaited_requests row of every orchestration that ran a
# 6,484 rows across 1,019 orchestrations. Deliberately WIDER than the 20 wedges: it carries
# the healthy population too, so the controls stay reproducible after the delete — the
# 20-wedged vs 11-never-advanced comparison and the healthy-continuation control both need
# rows that are not themselves wedges.
# FORMAT: tab-separated, NO header row, NO footer. Columns in order:
# Lines beginning '#' are commentary; every other line is exactly one row.
# ⚠ EXPORT INTEGRITY — READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANY RE-EXPORT. `kubectl exec … psql > file`
# TRUNCATES INTERMITTENTLY on an output this size, with no error inside the file and a
# perfectly well-formed final line. Measured 2026-08-20 across three attempts of the SAME
# command: 4,243 rows, then 5,186, then 6,484. A short export therefore reads as complete
# and its shortfall varies run to run. This file was accepted only on an explicit
# `[ "$n" -eq 6484 ]` assertion. ALWAYS assert the expected row count against the DB before
# using an export; never judge one by whether its tail looks sane.
# PROVEN TO RECONSTRUCT (2026-08-20, from this file alone, not from the DB):
#   20 wedged (next spawn present, next call_handler ABSENT) — all 08-17
#   11 never-advanced (no next spawn at all) — 10 on 08-17, 1 on 08-15
#    0 recovered.  The zero is the finding; the healthy population is the control.
# Rebuild with RECONSTRUCTION_QUERY.sql's logic: an iter_N_call_handler at
# retry_version>=3 AND status='error', the following iter_{N+1}_spawn_handler, and no
# CAVEAT: awaited_requests ONLY. orchestration_states was already purged when this was
# taken, so collected_data, last_activity and the reaper's error strings are NOT here and
# are not recoverable. Any figure quoting last_activity cannot be re-derived from this file.
